findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby/ERB syntax, causing template compilation to fail when rendering an existing embedded topic.
app/models/post.rb:132; app/models/topic_embed.rb:17-23 — Remote RSS content is stored as raw HTML and returned without sanitization, enabling stored XSS through malicious feed HTML.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — `postMessage` uses the full referrer URL as `targetOrigin` instead of an origin, causing resize messages from normal path-containing referrers to be rejected or throw.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14; app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — Cache misses enqueue retrieval jobs before throttling, and per-full-URL throttling can be bypassed by spoofing Referer and varying query strings to flood Sidekiq.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Substring origin matching allows controlled prefix domains to pass the origin check, so resize messages should require parsed exact-origin equality.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42-45 — The spec expects synchronous `TopicRetriever` instantiation and invocation even though the implementation enqueues `:retrieve_topic`, so it fails and does not test the actual asynchronous behavior.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14; app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — Cache misses enqueue retrieval jobs before throttling, and per-full-URL throttling can be bypassed by spoofing Referer and varying query strings to flood Sidekiq.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security concern in the diff. Looking at embed_controller.rb:14, when topic_id is nil, it enqueues a RetrieveTopic job. The throttling in topic_retriever.rb (retrieved_recently?) uses the full embed_url as the key, meaning different query strings create different throttle keys. The referer check in ensure_embeddable only validates the host matches embeddable_host, but an attacker could craft many different embed_urls with varying query parameters that all pass validation but each bypass the per-URL throttle, potentially flooding Sidekiq with retrieval jobs. This is a legitimate rate-limiting bypass vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42-45 — The spec expects synchronous `TopicRetriever` instantiation and invocation even though the implementation enqueues `:retrieve_topic`, so it fails and does not test the actual asynchronous behavior.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the EmbedController#best method (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:8-18) shows that when no topic_id is found, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` which is asynchronous. However, the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42-45 expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` to be called directly during the controller action. The actual implementation enqueues a job (Jobs::RetrieveTopic in app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) which then calls TopicRetriever. So the test is mocking the wrong thing - it expects synchronous TopicRetriever instantiation but the controller actually enqueues an async job. This test would fail because TopicRetriever.new is never called directly in the controller.
